text: Expanded/richer gallery comments feature (recurring internal ask, raised again with screenshot)
Unwatermarked web-quality (low-res, ~1600–2048px) digital download option (Pic-Time offers this); internally suggested to tie into configurable pricing per quality tier
Surface buyer's name/email in the download data sent to the photographer (today only captured for internal analytics when "require email" is on)
Tiered/package pricing for digital downloads — e.g. 1 photo for €5, 5 for €15, all for €40 — instead of only "buy 1" or "buy all"
Automated gallery population during tethered shooting: live culling/editing straight into an existing branded gallery, shareable via QR code during the shoot
French-language support for automatic order confirmation emails (currently English-only)
More gallery-creation/management settings inside the app itself, so photographers don't have to build galleries on the web and upload separately
Self-serve client photo selection + one-time-use coupon codes so clients can pick & check out their package's included image count on their own time (plus more coupon/promo code options)
Let photographers show the collection name persistently in the grid/frame instead of only on hover
Validate email addresses on gallery entry — or make it a toggleable "require valid email" option rather than a hard requirement (internal pushback on enforcing it outright)
Ability for photographers to request deletion of already-generated facial recognition data, plus clearer documentation of retention period / when it's created
Global toggle to turn off face recognition / AI Selfie Search across all galleries at once (currently must be disabled gallery-by-gallery)
Support connecting/importing photos from Google Drive and Dropbox into Galleries
Add an Australian print lab option

Automated gallery expiration & renewal flow: expiry-warning emails that let the client pay to auto-extend hosting, plus a "pay to reactivate" option on an expired gallery link (photographer also notified, with an option to reactivate for free)
More flexible, animated gallery layouts, similar to Pic-Time's sample galleries
Webhooks for gallery events (e.g. firing when a gallery is published) to automate CRM/delivery workflows
Ability to duplicate/copy an existing gallery
Apply separate watermark PNGs by image orientation (portrait vs landscape)
CRM & invoicing integration (client invoicing, contracts/waivers) within Aftershoot
Direct signup form on aftershoot.com/galleries with auto-login into galleries.aftershoot.com
Global privacy control: hide/disable the public gallery portal, make new galleries "Unlisted" by default, toggle visibility per gallery
Let users set an actual sale price for markups, not just a % markup (per Zenfolio example)
Save reusable gallery settings presets (download/email/visibility defaults per shoot type)
Shop/storefront UX overhaul: visible SHOP icon + multi-select images for cart/purchase
Support camera-to-phone uploads without needing a PC (FTP/mobile upload)
Let clients customize the background color of the photo-viewing area (competitor reference: CloudSpot)
Lock the gallery banner's aspect ratio so it doesn't crop on mobile, allow "text customization" to be left blank, and add a drop-shadow option for banner text

Vendor/client photo "sets": hidden or visible photo sets shareable via a direct link only (e.g. giving a wedding vendor like a florist or DJ access to just their relevant photos), with a single image able to live in multiple sets

Rich link preview when sharing a Gallery link with clients — show the gallery title + cover thumbnail (e.g. "Mrunal & Swetha Photo Collection by Mithunam Stories") instead of a bare URL; currently not possible, logged as ONCL-13374 (Selected for dev)
Support alternative payment methods for international customers (e.g. LINK for Philippine Pesos — PayPal is the only option today) (via website feedback)
Ability to set a limit on digital downloads, with clients able to purchase extra images individually or in bundles
Export client comments on gallery images as a list (to share with retouchers, instead of manual copy-paste)
Role-based/team access to galleries, so team members don't need full account credentials
Show brand logo (instead of plain text) at the top of gallery-share emails
Ability to remove/delete the face in the "AI selfie" feature (end-user feedback, submitted in French)
Album creation UX: let users name an album right after creating it (on the import screen, before photos are uploaded) and keep the album-name edit (pencil) icon visible at all times
Auto-create a public portfolio/landing page for every photographer (e.g. aftershoot.com/<name>) — even those who only use RAW Editing/Export — to help with SEO and seed usage
Build basic CRM capabilities (client relations, project tracking) integrated with Gallery/portfolio sharing, raised while comparing to competitors like HoneyBook
A test/sample purchase mode (no real payment) to verify a watermarked gallery delivers the un-watermarked image after checkout — currently not possible
Automated, time-based gallery sales (e.g. a discount for the first 10 days, another at expiration — like Instagram's scheduled sales) (x3 mentions, same customer thread)
Customizable gallery welcome/cover page design — the mobile welcome page shows an intentionally blurred background and a photographer asked if the page design could be made customizable/improved
Option to show no text overlay on the gallery cover photo
Recalculate/auto-fix the gallery cover photo so it isn't blurry
Built-in CRM with contracts + client login (competitor cited: Sprout Studio)
Bulk-select multiple photos to order prints with the same size/paper specs in Store (currently one at a time)
Full-resolution zoom on mobile gallery view (like Google Photos)
Let photographers assign a gallery to a collection directly while selecting a brand kit / creating the gallery
More LatAm payment methods — offline/cash, digital wallets (Nequi/DaviPlata), PSE bank transfer
Password-protect sub-albums/collections within a gallery, so each person (e.g. multi-headshot session) only accesses their own section with a password
Per-client download analytics should count all media types, not just photo/album downloads (video downloads currently missing)
Video gallery enhancements for hybrid shooters: photo-only/video-only/both gallery modes, custom video display names, dedicated video cover photo
API for automated/automatic photo uploads into Galleries
Allow disabling full-gallery downloads while letting clients self-select favorites and check out a limited number of digital downloads (Zenfolio-style workflow)
Centralized analytics dashboard across all galleries (views/downloads/engagement in one place)
Customizable client delivery emails — button colors/fonts and a less generic "View Gallery" CTA
Customizable fonts for set headings to match the main gallery header
Higher-resolution gallery cover images (team says a fix is already rolling out)
Square (non-rounded) image corners option for the gallery grid
Standalone option to pay for gallery migration without needing a full Galleries plan
(Internal/eng) Track errors from the core edit+retouch pipeline in PostHog, not just upload/cloud errors, to gauge their blast radius on Gallery
Bulk-select & purchase multiple photos surfaced via AI face-recognition search (checkout currently forces one-by-one selection)
Custom/required checkout fields (e.g. bib number, name) for photo orders
GBP (multi-currency) pricing & checkout for the Galleries storefront — currently USD-only; open points are Stripe's cross-currency fee and refund-rate drift
Nested sub-folder hierarchy for organizing galleries (3–5+ levels deep), requested by a photographer migrating from SmugMug
One-click "buy all my photos" package via AI face/bib-number recognition, similar to Sportograf
Ability to expand/enlarge horizontal images in a gallery, like Pic Time offers
Gallery slideshows should loop instead of stopping after the last image
Let photographers see/export a list of guest favorites (platform comparison: Zenfolio)
PIN-protect an individual set within a gallery, so only guests with the PIN can view that set while the rest stay open to everyone
Toggle gallery watermark on/off without needing to re-upload all images
Add email notifications when someone views/accesses a gallery (competitor reference: Picflow)
Add more spacing/padding between the watermark logo and the image edge (currently sits too close to the border)
Allow manually ordering galleries within a collection instead of forcing alphabetical order
Let photographers control/suppress the automatic Aftershoot "gallery download" email sent to their clients (caused client confusion about sign-up/payment)
Add WHCC custom cards to the Galleries print product lineup
Add a New Zealand print lab (e.g. Queensberry) to Galleries
Let clients selectively download just one album/section of a gated gallery instead of the whole gallery
Allow selling web-size print files without watermark
Coupon to let a client check out a subset of a larger gallery for $0, instead of photographer manually rebuilding a downloadable album
Default the "Almost There" download pop-up/PIN to off, so clients can one-click download
Event Date field: allow backdating to past dates for older galleries (noted as fixed same-day in thread)
Gallery banner: lock aspect ratio so sponsor logos display consistently across device sizes
Print store checkout: only show clients the sizes/papers the photographer has enabled, instead of the full WHCC catalog shown (greyed out)
Print store pricing editor: add a "Check All / Uncheck All" toggle for product/size visibility
Store coupons: support a flat dollar-amount discount, not just percentage-based
Discount codes with an expiry date in the Galleries store
In-app promotional nudges (top banner + sidebar plan card) for the Black Friday campaign
Let clients submit feedback on photos and have Aftershoot auto-suggest/apply the edit for approval (e.g. "remove my wrinkles")
Move a photo between albums within a gallery (e.g. promote into Highlights after the fact)
Multi-currency support (e.g. GBP display, not just USD) in the Galleries store
Password-protect/block downloads for videos and add a watermark overlay during video playback
Search photos by text/numbers on tagged items (e.g. race bib numbers) or by dominant color, similar to face search
"Coming soon" gallery preview with QR code guest selfie registration + notify-when-photos-ready (like FotoOwl)
A print lab option that ships internationally (e.g. to Australia)
Booking/appointment module for photo shoots (e.g. couple consultations)
Bulk option to hide/disable multiple store products at once (currently one-by-one only)
Embed a gallery via an HTML code snippet on external blogs/websites (like Pic-Time)
Mobile app / easier way to access galleries and grab share links from phone
Multi-currency support for digital image sales (GBP for UK sellers)
Automatic "Contact Form" on gallery pages so visitors can leave email/phone for campaigns & CRM
Slideshow feature for galleries, like Pic-Time has
Add star ratings (3/4/5★) alongside the existing Heart/Favorite selection, so clients can tag photos for different deliverables (prints/album sizes)
Built-in CRM for Aftershoot Galleries (contracts, invoices, gallery delivery in one place)
Make the Aftershoot logo/home link in the Galleries sidebar open in a new tab via mouse-wheel/middle-click (to quickly open multiple Galleries tabs)
Option to restrict/limit gallery downloads to specific people (e.g. only the couple), to protect print/download revenue
Sort favorited/selected photo numbers in ascending numerical order when exporting a selection list
Support 100% discount codes on Galleries so specific people (e.g. a social media contact) get free, watermark-free access while others pay
Add mobile money support (e.g. M-Pesa) as a payment method for regions without Stripe access (customer specifically flagged Kenya)
Improve culling/selection to avoid picking near-duplicate images that have closed eyes or low quality
Client self-booking for galleries, similar to ShootProof's "Book clients"
Let clients explicitly confirm their final favorites selection, with an email notification sent to the photographer
Let photographers set a max number of photos clients can select as favorites
Lightroom Classic Publish Service for Galleries — map LrC collections to galleries/sets, auto-replace re-edited images on republish, control export size/settings, preserve sort order
Mobile app to manage galleries on-the-go (toggle settings like downloads, respond to clients quickly)
Slideshow/video maker with music, 4K export, and configurable photos-per-slide matching brand theme
Ability to edit/retouch client-favorited images directly from the gallery, plus a search button to find images in a gallery
Ability to selectively hide/remove individual store products (e.g. leather albums) without disabling the whole vendor
Centralized/easier cross-gallery activity notifications & analytics (one feed showing all galleries' activity, incl. login dates), vs. digging into each gallery separately
Customizable/universal text translations across the gallery page (edit all labels/copy in own language and style)
Freely position gallery name/title on the cover (not limited to preset positions)
Global default gallery settings (downloads, privacy, resolution) reusable across all galleries, beyond what Brand Kit covers today
Organize gallery images into sections/folders (Highlights, Getting Ready, Ceremony, Reception, Portraits)
Photographer mobile web access to manage/share galleries (e.g. text a gallery link from a phone browser instead of emailing it to self)
Album templates and layouts for reveal sessions (cited Fundy)
Built-in website builder for photographers (cited Pixieset)
Localized/translated gallery delivery pages — Dutch and Portuguese requested
Mobile-friendly client access — let clients view/open their gallery from their phone (cited Pixieset as having this)
More design options for the gallery cover page
RAW file support for gallery delivery (cited Pixieset)
Cap/limit free downloads in a gallery package — e.g. allow only 10–20 free images per gallery before requiring payment for the rest (already tracked as Gating V2, ONCL-14140)
Activity notifications for gallery owners (order placed, downloaded, favorited), like Pixieset
Full website/landing-page builder beyond gallery pages, so photographers can migrate their whole site to Aftershoot
Guided album design/sales workflow for selling printed albums & wall art
Mobile app (or mobile-friendly access) for clients to view galleries, like Pic-Time offers
Raise the ~10-recipient limit when sending/sharing a gallery via email
Simplify how watermarks are configured/displayed in Galleries
Support deferred-payment checkout (order now, pay via a separate invoice e.g. QuickBooks) for gallery orders
White-label print store with the photographer's own commission, shareable as a standalone print link
Hide the "Photos By" attribution text in the gallery footer — no setting exists today in the footer editor or Brand Kit

Predefined/default gallery settings (a template or preset) so photographers don't have to reconfigure the same options for every new client gallery — customer compared favorably to Pixieset, which has this, while evaluating a move to Galleries
Support $0/zero-valued store packages (e.g. "3 included digital downloads per family" with paid extras) — confirmed as currently unsupported
Auto-email the feedback submitter whenever a teammate replies in the feedback Slack thread (like the Blaze bot does for support)
Dark mode option for the gallery grid/viewing experience
Guest photo-upload via a shareable QR/link (a separate "Guests" section alongside Photos/Videos) for wedding guests to add their own photos
More prominent/bold hamburger-menu icon on the Galleries page (currently near-invisible)
Per-collection visual branding/style customization (today Brand Kits only apply at the gallery level) — customer has been waiting months
Redesigned collections view: smaller thumbnails with event title shown underneath (cited Pixieset)
Save gallery settings as a reusable preset/template (cited Pixieset) so galleries don't need to be built from scratch each time
Support subfolders/categories when uploading photos into a gallery (e.g. splitting a wedding reception into portraits, group photos, etc.)
